episode_row: gpt-5.6-sol audit latent batch (F2 projected-DD early lock ×11 no harm; F3; F4; F6 realized_calibration dead in prod; F8; F10 derivation lost; F12 unit drift; F13 scoring race; F15; R4)

commits.subject: fix(cli): preview default 'tomorrow' in ET, not UTC (audit F15)
commits.body:
Between ~8pm and midnight ET, utcnow()+1day targets the day AFTER tomorrow,
so a manual evening/recovery preview wrote the wrong slate. Same class as the
O2 _today_et fix; new _tomorrow_et mirrors it. Tests plant resolved picks at
both candidate dates on disk (no load_pick mock — import-during-patch leaks
poisoned unrelated tests) plus a run_pipeline tripwire so a date regression
fails fast instead of hitting the live data refresh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(health): let unexpected check crashes reach _safe_run → CRITICAL (audit F4)
commits.body:
calibration, projected_lineup, post_failure, disk_fill caught Exception
internally and returned [] — an evaluation failure was indistinguishable from
healthy, structurally defeating _safe_run's promised CRITICAL-on-crash (the
audit-H3 fix). Expected data-absence paths (empty dirs, per-file corruption
skips in the lookback scan) stay quiet; two legacy tests encoding the
swallow behavior flipped to the propagation contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): atomic state save, corrupt-state quarantine, READY after state init (audit F3)
commits.body:
save_state used bare write_text on the exact file startup parses
crash-unprotected — a torn write meant a 30s crash-restart loop that stayed
externally green (heartbeat + READY were signaled before state was touched,
any fresh 'running' heartbeat scores healthy, the restart-spike check runs
only at EOD inside the crashing process, and the deploy canary is is-active
at +30s). Now: atomic_write_text (the util docstring described this exact
class), corrupt files quarantined to *.corrupt-<ts> with evidence preserved
and startup degrading to fresh state, and load_state runs before
notify_ready so a failing init can never advertise liveness.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(health): quarantine visibility + external restart-churn detection (audit F3)
commits.body:
scheduler_state_integrity source WARNs while a *.corrupt-* quarantine is
recent (day-state was reset; evidence file preserved). check_heartbeat gains
an NRestarts sampler: +3 restarts inside 20 min is treated exactly like a
stale heartbeat (fail ping) — a 30s crash-loop refreshes the heartbeat every
cycle, so freshness alone scores a crash-loop healthy. Counter resets
rebaseline instead of firing; unreadable systemctl skips quietly (churn is an
addition to the liveness signal, never a breaker). Defaults activate via the
existing cron line — no cron change needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(health): realized_calibration pools by regime fingerprint, not deploy wall-clock (audit F6)
commits.body:
Every deploy stamp (11 in 10 days: docs, shadow, ops) reset the calibration
sample, so min_bucket_n was never reached and the check was dead exactly
during active development. Picks already stamp model_pickle_sha256 /
policy_npz_sha256 / feature_env_hash; the pool is now all in-window picks
matching the newest stamped pick's fingerprint — no-regime-change deploys
keep the sample, genuine model/policy/env changes still reset it, and
unstamped pre-provenance picks fall back to the wall-clock filter (runner
signature unchanged).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(leaderboard): gzip static snapshots + per-day bytes telemetry (review F14/#14)
commits.body:
Raw JSON snapshots accumulated ~190 MB/day unbounded (players/ alone 879MB).
New snapshots store as .json.gz (dedupe stays keyed on the RAW sha, so
capture behavior is unchanged; nothing in prod reads the archive back) and
capture_status.json gains bytes_day/bytes_stored_today so the trajectory is
observable. Existing plain-JSON backlog left as-is; retention policy
deferred until the compressed slope warrants it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(scoring): shared flock serializes daemon vs 1am-cron streak scoring (review F13/#13)
commits.body:
Both scorers do load daily -> resolve -> update_streak -> save_pick on the
same date around 01:00 ET with no lock (only saver state had one); an
interleave could double-apply or lose a streak update. New
picks.scoring_lock (flock on data/picks/.scoring.lock) wraps the
read-modify-write at all three sites — check-results, the daemon's mid-game
early path, and its all-final path — each re-loading the pick INSIDE the
lock and skipping if a peer already scored (red test demonstrated the
double-count: streak 7 vs correct 6). Resolution stays outside the lock
(idempotent network read); the critical section is sub-second.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(scoring): review round 2 — every result writer now locked and clobber-safe (Codex #1,#4,#5,#6,#8,#9)
commits.body:
The cheap-fixes review went deeper into the pre-existing writer set: the
daemon's cap/unresolved-final/suspended branches wrote stale objects
unlocked (a cron-scored terminal hit could be overwritten with
unresolved/suspended) — now routed through save_nonterminal_result, a
locked reload-that-refuses-to-clobber-terminal. The 2am reconcile_results
(writer of BOTH pick files and streak.json, racing the daemon until 05:00)
now resolves boxscores unlocked, then applies corrections + the season
replay under scoring_lock against reloaded state. All scoring sites adopt
the FRESH pick before mutating (concurrent metadata updates survive) and
fail closed when the file vanished mid-flight. Shadow reconciliation moved
outside the lock (network under a global lock). checkout gets
persist-credentials:false; ARCHITECTURE documents the mixed .json/.json.gz
archive. Deferred (with rationale): two-file streak+pick atomicity journal
(pre-existing, healed by reconcile + contest anchoring), public-mode reply
dedup (dormant — prod is DM mode), telemetry undercount on kill-mid-capture.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(health): canonical systemd unit templates + read-only drift check (audit F12)
commits.body:
The tracked scheduler unit was the stale Pi5 one (/home/stonehengee,
Type=simple, on-failure/300s) while prod runs notify+watchdog/always/30s
— DR from the repo would have installed a broken unit, and live edits
could drift unreviewed.

- scripts/systemd/{bts-scheduler,bts-dashboard}.service: byte-identical
  captures of the live units (sha256-verified against the box).
- unit_drift health source (Tier 3, repeated-attention): WARNs on
  installed-vs-template divergence or an installed tracked unit with no
  template; silent off-box. Read-only by design.
- scripts/install-systemd-hetzner.sh: explicit operator install/diff,
  never enables or restarts (restarts belong to the deploy canary).
- Removed the stale scripts/bts-scheduler.service.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(sync): content-addressed R2 keys make the manifest flip the only commit point (audit F8)
commits.body:
The old protocol overwrote stable keys in place BEFORE replacing the
manifest: an interrupted sync left the old manifest pointing at new
bytes — the backup was inconsistent during exactly the failure window
it exists to survive, and verify_manifest only looked at metadata/age.

- Changed files upload to objects/<sha256>/<name>; a prior manifest's
  bytes are never overwritten. Unchanged entries are preserved verbatim,
  so the existing legacy-layout objects stay restorable without churn.
- sync_from_r2 downloads to a .part temp, verifies the checksum, then
  os.replace()s — a corrupt download can no longer destroy a good local
  file (previously it deleted the freshly-written dest in place).
- verify_manifest now HEADs every referenced object (existence + size),
  reported as objects_ok; CLI exits 1 on failure.
- prune_unreferenced: deletes objects/ keys the current manifest no
  longer references, only when older than 7d (age guard protects
  in-flight syncs); legacy keys / manifest / raw-archive tarball are
  structurally out of scope. Runs after sync-to-r2 (--no-prune to skip).

Regression test reproduces the audit scenario: uploads succeed, manifest
publish crashes → restore from the surviving manifest returns the old
bytes exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(strategy): early lock requires the selected double-down confirmed too (audit F2)
commits.body:
The gap rule is valid for a single pick racing projected alternatives,
but the scheduler applied it unchanged to double days: a projected DD
rode through on the primary's confirmation (11 production days, 4
locked 51-133min early; 0 realized scratches — this is tail insurance
against displacement, per Eric's call 2026-07-10).

should_lock gains an optional double_down slot; _lock_decision_from_
predictions passes it on double days. Coverage flows to the in-loop
fallback deferral automatically (same helper); the T-35 final fallback
deliberately bypasses should_lock, so the gate can only delay delivery
within the day, never lose it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(skip-shadow): version the 0.744 derivation + pre-registered verdict checkpoints (audit F10)
commits.body:
The breakeven's derivation lived only at /tmp/skip_qdelta.py on the box
— confirmed gone. scripts/audit/skip_breakeven_derivation.py re-derives
it from repo artifacts (Q(single)==Q(skip) on the calibrated
estimated-PA value function, both objectives, sweeping n_bins/horizon/
saver): reach57 median p* 0.7418, E[max] 0.7485 — reproducing the
recorded ~0.744 (0.742-0.752). Constant unchanged: it sits inside the
re-derived band, and moving a pre-registered threshold mid-experiment
is itself a peeking sin. Inputs fingerprinted in
docs/audit/2026-07-10-skip-breakeven-derivation.json.

Verdict statistics fixed: nightly re-testing a fixed-N 95% Wilson CI is
not time-uniform — repeated looks inflate the chance a transient
crossing gets presented as 'skip validated/costs streaks'. Verdicts now
come only from pre-registered looks at n∈{30,60,90} resolved divergent
days (Bonferroni z=2.394 per look), each computed deterministically
from the first-c records in date order so the stateless nightly rebuild
replays identical looks; a decisive look is terminal. The running
Wilson CI stays in the status as monitoring display. Status schema v2
(+verdict_basis); dashboard/CLI consumers read the same keys.

Records now carry the (policy_npz_sha256, feature_env_hash) regime
fingerprint (same identity as realized_calibration/F6) for future
stratification — the breakeven is one model era's number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix: round-2 adversarial review — 11 findings on the fix batch + ops work
commits.body:
gpt-5.6-sol against everything unreviewed since round 1 (the round-1
fixes themselves, the CI environment work) plus the recovered morning
full-batch report. Fixed:

- R1  a failed backup run discarded the last successful snapshot_id, so
      restore-drill regressed to 'latest --tag ops' — the exact partial-
      snapshot condition the I4 fix was for. last_success_snapshot_id
      now survives failures; the drill prefers it unconditionally
- R2  INCIDENT box-loss runbook restores by drill-verified snapshot ID,
      never latest
- R3  prev-manifest preservation now FAILS CLOSED: a failed copy aborts
      the sync (retry next run) instead of publishing a manifest whose
      outgoing generation is immediately pruneable under a reader
- R4  the lock decision revalidates BOTH selected slots against the
      fresh game-status snapshot — a primary whose game went postponed
      between selection and lock no longer rides its stale lineup flag
      into delivery (contender rows were filtered; the committed slots
      were not)
- R5  prune_superseded is age-fenced to the checkpoint-eligibility
      window: the same-day-flip assumption is now ENFORCED, so a fired
      pre-registered look's membership is provably immutable
- R6  deploy concurrency queues instead of cancelling: run-level
      cancellation fires BEFORE the job-level environment gate, so a
      mistaken main-branch dispatch could kill an in-flight deploy
      mid-SSH and strand the box without its canary/rollback
- R7  probe audits take the saver flock (trail order = attempt order)
- #4  audit-append failures now log loudly (the trail IS the F7
      accepted-risk control; a swallowed append = unaudited mutation)
- #10 dashboard + CLI show the verdict's own pre-registered-look basis
      (n, hits, CI, z) and label the running Wilson CI monitoring-only
      — the juxtaposition invited misreads
- #11 unit_drift WARNs on symlinked units (hash equality proves nothing
      about systemd's loaded definition)
- #5  verify-manifest output labeled 'existence+size only; restores
      verify sha256'

Accepted with rationale (audit doc): fresh-box bootstrap remains a
documented runbook step (absent-status-silent convention stands);
deeper postponed-commit hardening already has a Tier-1 health source.

Suite 1796 -> 1801.
